scenes.title: Break the fantasy loop, then build skill
scenes.sub: A learning video made from your research report
scenes.say: This video turns your research report into something you can learn from. It covers maladaptive daydreaming, the music that feeds it, and how to learn and build the skills your work needs.

scenes.head: The map
items: What it costs, and success fantasies
scenes.say: Here is the map. Chapters one to four cover maladaptive daydreaming: what it is, six ways of seeing it, the loop that drives it, and what it costs. Chapter five looks at your playlist. Chapters six to eight cover learning, skill, and your actual work. Chapter nine is a practical protocol, and chapter ten is a recap quiz.

scenes.head: How to use this video
items: ‘Pause and recall’: answer before the reveal. Testing yourself beats rereading.
Evidence badges: A strongest · B strong, related · C weak or qualitative · D untested
Watch one or two chapters at a time. Spacing beats bingeing.
Pause to write your own example. Producing beats watching.
scenes.say: A few rules for watching. When you see pause and recall, actually try to answer before the reveal. Testing yourself beats rereading. The badge in the top corner shows how strong the evidence is: A is strongest, D is untested inference. Watch one or two chapters at a time, because spacing beats bingeing. And pause to write your own example, because producing beats watching.

scenes.text: Almost all MD research comes from *one network of researchers*, mostly with *online volunteers*. That's why claims carry ~evidence labels~.
scenes.say: One honest caveat before we start. Almost all MD research comes from one network of researchers: Somer in Haifa, Soffer-Dudek at Ben-Gurion University, and their collaborators. Most of it recruits self-identified sufferers online, about three-quarters of them women. That does not make the findings wrong. It is why so many claims carry an evidence label.
